title: Girl Power in Scary Movies: More Women Are Directing Horror and Fantasy Films!
summary: Have you ever watched a scary movie or a wild fantasy film and wondered who dreamed it up? For a long time, most directors of these "genre" films—horror, fantasy, sci-fi—were men. But things are changing! At a recent film market in Costa Rica, Monica Garcia, the boss of the Sitges Film Festival in Spain, shared some exciting news. Six years ago, only 6% of genre directors at her festival were women. Now, that number has jumped to about 30%! That's a huge leap, thanks partly to a program called WomanInFan that supports female filmmakers. But even with this progress, women still face obstacles. Garcia showed a documentary where women directors talked about their struggles. One was Katharina Kubrick, daughter of the legendary director Stanley Kubrick. She said she was pushed aside just for being a woman and Kubrick's daughter. "It's not a generational thing," Garcia said. "It's something that has lasted for decades." The panel also talked about what makes Latin American fantasy special. Pablo Guisa, a film producer, said the shared culture of saints, demons, and miracles is "perfect fuel for genre cinema." He pointed to famous directors like Guillermo del Toro as examples. Mexican director Luis Javier Henaine, whose horror film "Disappear Completely" is getting rave reviews, shared his secret: he focuses on real human emotions first, and the scares or laughs follow naturally. So, who's the next big thing? Garcia said they're eagerly waiting for the next Issa López, the director of "Tigers Are Not Afraid," to make another film. The message is clear: the door is open wider than ever, and the world is ready for more thrilling stories from women's imaginations.
why_it_matters: When you watch movies, seeing women directors means you get new kinds of stories, and it shows that anyone, no matter their gender, can dream up thrilling adventures.

background_read: For many years, most scary and fantasy movies were directed by men. The Sitges Film Festival (a big festival in Spain that celebrates these kinds of films) used to have very few women directors. Stanley Kubrick (a legendary director of famous movies like 'The Shining') had a daughter, Katharina, who struggled to be accepted as a filmmaker. Latin American culture, full of stories about saints and miracles, has inspired directors like Guillermo del Toro (who won Oscars for 'The Shape of Water').
Article_Structure: WHO: Monica Garcia, film directors, and producers.
WHAT: More women are now directing horror and fantasy movies.
WHERE: The talk happened at a film market in Costa Rica, but the change is happening worldwide.
WHY: Programs like WomanInFan are helping, and audiences want fresh stories, showing that women's imaginations are powerful.

perspectives.description: Having more women direct horror and fantasy adds fresh ideas and makes these films more interesting for everyone.
Even with progress, women still face being pushed aside just because of their gender, as Katharina Kubrick's story shows.
With programs like WomanInFan, the next generation of girls can be inspired to tell their own scary and magical stories on the big screen.
